pred_ddx.label: Benign lymphoid lesion in the pancreas

Benign lymphoid lesion in the pancreas: The patient's history of hepatitis C, the presence of a well-defined mass in the head of the pancreas, and the histopathological features of the lesion, including hyperplastic lymph nodes and normal distribution of T and B cell markers, support this diagnosis.
Reactive lymphoid hyperplasia: The presence of hyperplastic lymph nodes, marked vascular proliferation, and hyalinization of germinal centers, along with the absence of markers indicative of lymphoid malignancies, also support a diagnosis of reactive lymphoid hyperplasia.
